body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It was a hard Halloween weekend in this county — four people died in four separate incidents across the city in less than 22 hours, and a Wasco barricade kept police busy into the night. Today brings a little quiet: a high near 68 under clear skies, moderate air quality, and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County. Take care of each other out there.

## The Kern Overnight

The night began with a standoff in Wasco, where police asked for a K9 unit at 8:49 p.m. for a man barricaded inside a home in the 2200 block of 3rd Street. He was wanted on a protective order violation. Earlier in the evening, at 7:40 p.m., a vehicle struck a cyclist at North Chester Avenue and Roberts Lane and kept going — the car described as a maroon or red Toyota with front-end damage and no bumper, last seen heading east on East Roberts Lane. A white Honda CR-V was later reported trying to pick up the missing bumper. Crews also handled a vehicle fire in the 3600 block of Sewell Street at 7:42 p.m., and Delano police responded to a rollover at 10:47 p.m. where a vehicle landed on its roof in the roadway with one patient reported.

The overnight hours turned domestic and violent. At 11:22 p.m., a man with a gun was reported threatening people near an auto shop. Eleven minutes later, officers were sent to the 5000 block of Pierce Road in north Bakersfield after a juvenile reported his mother had hit him with a meat cleaver; two juveniles were to be checked on. At 11:49 p.m., officers responded to the 1400 block of East 9th Street, where a victim was reported assaulted with an iron object. A fight between a man and a woman in the 3000 block of Glenwood was reported out of control at 12:41 a.m. Then came a priority domestic at 2:36 a.m. in the 8100 block of Seminole Court in southwest Bakersfield, where one person reported being cut with a box cutter and the other was reported sitting on a bed holding it. Two more priority domestic calls followed — the 300 block of Dr Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard at 2:50 a.m. and the 2900 block of Descanso Street at 3:08 a.m. A battery at a grocery store in the 7900 block of White Lane was reported at 3:58 a.m., and at 4:19 a.m. crews were sent to a market in the 9500 block of South Union Avenue, where a woman was reported to have set a fire at the back of the building and was being argumentative. Deputies also checked on three young children, ages three to six, reported outside with three adults at 7:19 p.m., and officers ran a welfare check at a motel on the frontage road at 7:31 p.m. for a man who called 911 saying he was scared.

## Today's weather

It's 50 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 68 and a low around 51 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires to report. Air quality sits at 61 — moderate — so most folks can go about their day normally, though sensitive readers may want to keep an eye on it if they're planning hard outdoor work this afternoon. Light layers this morning, short sleeves by lunch.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that a woman was killed in a shooting at a Halloween gathering in Bakersfield, one of four deaths across the city in a span of less than 22 hours.** According to 23ABC, the violence began just before 2:45 a.m. Saturday on White Lane, when a Bakersfield police officer driving to a call for service struck a woman who walked into the roadway outside a crosswalk; she was pronounced dead less than ten minutes later. Just after 3:30 a.m., police responded to gunfire near a large party on South Half Moon Drive and found a 16-year-old boy with major injuries — he died at the hospital, and police are still searching for suspects. On Halloween night, just after 6:30, a driver hit four pedestrians crossing in an unmarked crosswalk at Harris Road and Marin Street; a 12-year-old girl died, and the other three victims are recovering from injuries that don't appear life-threatening. The driver stayed at the scene and cooperated.

**Bakersfield Now reports that at least one person is believed to have been killed in an incident in Oildale, and that a woman was killed and two others injured in a shooting at a large gathering Sunday.** Just after 12:30 a.m. Sunday, Kern County Sheriff's deputies responded to reports of an armed robbery on Rosedale Highway, where hundreds of people were fleeing a large gathering after three women were shot; one of them was pronounced dead. The two weekend shootings and two crashes together account for four deaths in less than a day, a toll that has shaken neighborhoods across the city and left investigators working multiple active cases at once.

**23ABC reports that Dolores Huerta, the civil rights icon and co-founder of the United Farm Workers, has died at 96.** Her family says she died Wednesday morning at her home in southwest Bakersfield. Huerta's fight began in the 1960s in Delano, where she organized farmworkers alongside César Chávez and helped build a movement that reshaped lives across the Central Valley. Bakersfield College professor Olivia Garcia told the station that Huerta was "one of us" — a powerful Chicana the community got to share with the world. Kern County Supervisor Leticia Perez said Huerta mentored her, teaching her to see every door as an organizing opportunity, and longtime activist Lisa Buckner said the loss leaves a big hole in many lives. The family says plans to celebrate her life and legacy will follow.

## Something good

A Kern County nonprofit is working to educate Spanish-speaking voters about the propositions on the upcoming ballot, according to 23ABC. The effort is aimed at helping more residents understand what they're being asked to decide and take part in the election — the kind of quiet, patient work that strengthens a community one conversation at a time. If you know someone who'd welcome help understanding the ballot, this is a good week to point them toward it.

## Coming up this week

It's a full week of public business in Bakersfield. The City Council meets twice on Wednesday, November 4 — first at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. — and the Police Civil Service Commission meets that same morning at 8:30 a.m. Then on Thursday, November 5, the Planning Commission takes up its agenda at 5:30 p.m. If you've got thoughts on a project or a policy in your neighborhood, these are the rooms where those decisions get made, and the public is welcome.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch ahead. Journey USA plays the Fox on Saturday, November 7, with TEXAS TORNADO TRADITION also on the bill that same day. The Cults & Classics series continues with "Play Misty for Me" on Monday, November 9, followed by NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet on Friday, November 13, and the 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards on Sunday, November 15. Season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are also on sale now. Whatever your week holds, keep an eye on your neighbors — after a weekend like this one, a little extra kindness goes a long way.

top.title: Woman dead after shooting at Halloween gathering in Bakersfield
